title: The Dynamic Network Approach of Mental Health to Stimulate Innovations for Interventions and Changes - Core Assessment
summary: The Z-Project is part of the state-funded DYNAMIC research network in Hesse, Germany. Its goal is to better understand how mental disorders such as depression, anxiety or schizophrenia develop and change in daily life. Patients and healthy individuals take part. All participants complete a comprehensive baseline assessment including MRI, EEG, tests and questionnaires, together with three weeks of daily smartphone-based surveys. No treatment or medication is given. The study aims to better characterise patient subgroups and to identify early warning signs and improve future psychological and medical interventions.
conditions: The Z-Project includes adult patients with a broad range of psychiatric disorders. The primary focus is on affective disorders (particularly major depressive disorder) and anxiety or stress-related disorders. To enable a transdiagnostic network perspective, additional diagnostic groups are also eligible, including:  Depressive disorders (current or remitted major depressive episodes)  Anxiety disorders (e.g. generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder)  Trauma- and stressor-related disorders (e.g. PTSD, adjustment disorders)  Obsessive-compulsive and related disorders  Schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders  Bipolar disorders (if clinically stable and not in acute mania)  Additional psychiatric diagnoses may be included in justified cases if they  are not primarily due to an organic brain condition,  allow safe participation in MRI/EEG protocols, and  are clinically stable enough for study participation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients:

Age 18–70 years

DSM-5 diagnosis of a mental disorder (e.g. depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, PTSD, OCD, schizophrenia spectrum)

Clinical stability (no acute suicidality, mania, or psychotic crisis)

Sufficient German language skills and ability to provide informed consent

Willingness to participate

- Healthy controls:

Age 18–70 years

No current or past psychiatric disorder (according to mini DIPS)

No current psychotropic medication

Willing to participate
Exclusion criteria:
Organic brain disorders or neurological conditions (e.g., epilepsy, dementia, multiple sclerosis)

Severe cognitive impairment or lack of capacity to provide informed consent

Insufficient proficiency in the German language

Significant, non-correctable impairments in hearing or vision
